model.threshold_note: 0.90 chosen on calibration data only; see reports/field_v2_threshold_sweep.md

ship_decision.what: Human ship decision for the phone app's image model. The ship rule itself is computed by model/field_eval.py and model/field_threshold.py; this file only records what the team decided and why. Read by model/evaluate.py, model/field_eval.py and model/field_threshold.py when they render reports.
ship_decision.decided_by: the Cafetal team (an explicit human decision, not the output of the ship-rule script)
ship_decision.rule_outcome: The pre-registered ship rule says DO NOT SHIP: v2 at t = 0.90 passes 4 of its 5 conditions and misses one (reports/field_v2_threshold_test.json)
ship_decision.exception: (2), JMuBEN test macro-F1 (argmax and app-level) may drop at most 1 point
ship_decision.reason: the Kenyan close-ups it no longer answers go to the fail-safe "I'm not sure" (UNSR: show the leaf to the officer), not to wrong answers, and it never called a diseased leaf "sano" on either test set; and v2 is the only model that finds rust in field photos (v1 finds none on the held-out field test).
ship_decision.note: Wording of "reason" updated on 2026-10-04 for the Kenya/English re-localization: the fail-safe is now quoted by its English text and SMS code ("I'm not sure", UNSR). The decision, its date and its grounds are unchanged; the earlier wording is in git history.

reference.name: v1
reference.note: the app's previous model, evaluated on the same images, decided with its own threshold

field_test.note: 0 images - not yet collected (put photos in data/field_test/<label>/ and rerun)

leakage_check.note: unused copies (flips/rotations/colour shifts/burst shots) of TRAINING photos, i.e. what a naive random split would have put in the test set. Compare with the group-split test.

inat_coffee_photos.note: iNatAg-mini/coffea_arabica (iNaturalist, CC BY-NC 4.0): whole plants, flowers, cherries; disease status unknown. Not used for training (neither v1 nor v2). Desired behaviour: mostly DUDA.

inat_field.note: held-out field test only (observers not used in training, except the observer of 1 American leaf spot photo); iNaturalist photos are a proxy for field photos from Kirinyaga, and none of the labelled disease photos is from East Africa; details, ship rule and v1/v2 comparison in reports/field_eval.md

size_latency.latency_note: onnxruntime Python 1.19.2, CPUExecutionProvider, 1 thread, batch 1, median of 50, build server x86 CPU (not a phone)
size_latency.ortweb_note: onnxruntime-web 1.19.2 WASM backend, 1 thread, Node.js on the build server (not a phone), measured at export time (model/export_onnx.py, calibration record)
size_latency.download_note: computed = bytes*8/bitrate, no protocol overhead; throttled-browser measurements are in reports/browser_metrics.md (emulated)

data_split.hash: dHash 72-bit on equalised grayscale 9x9, min over 8 flips/rotations, Hamming <= 8, union-find

threshold.floor_reason: validation images come from the same Kenyan dataset as training, so confidence on real field photos will be lower and less reliable; the floor keeps the PLAN.md default 0.70 when the data-driven value is lower
threshold.rule: lowest t in [0.50,0.90] where accepted validation predictions reach >= 95% accuracy on clean images AND on clean + 5 phone-like degradations (jpeg q25, blur r2, brightness x0.6/x1.4, downscale 64); blur-rejected images count as not accepted

blur_threshold.rule: floor(min over coffee classes of the 5th percentile of real validation images), 1 decimal
